author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Calibrate analog trigger range for PS2 input
summary: Observe released, partial, and fully pressed L2 and R2 values, remove duplicate digital bindings, set only the minimum supported threshold needed, and prove gradual travel plus full activation after reconnect.
heroAlt: PCSX2 automatic controller mapping screen showing detected gamepad and binding controls

sourceLabels.android-game-controller: Android controller events, axes, and device behavior

blocks.text: Prove the released and full endpoints separately

Android controllers may expose each trigger as an independent axis, a shared axis, a digital button, or both. A trigger that never reaches zero can behave as permanently held, while one that never reaches maximum can fail driving or action checks. Use a live input display and press L2 and R2 slowly through their complete travel. Record endpoints before changing thresholds.
Do not bind both the analog axis and its duplicate digital code to the same PS2 trigger unless the device documentation and test prove that combination is required.
Prepare an endpoint and travel test

items: Controller in one documented Android input mode.
Live raw or normalized trigger values visible.
Existing trigger bindings and thresholds recorded.
A game action that recognizes partial pressure where available.
A second action that clearly requires full trigger activation.

blocks.text: Map one trigger axis at a time

items: 1. Release both triggers and record their stable neutral values.
2. Press L2 slowly to full travel and note direction, minimum, maximum, and any digital event.
3. Repeat the measurement for R2.
4. Remove duplicate button entries that cause immediate full activation.
5. Apply the smallest supported threshold correction only when neutral noise requires it.
6. Verify several partial positions in the live tester.
7. Test partial and full actions in gameplay without changing sensitivity.
8. Reconnect and confirm both endpoints plus gradual travel remain stable.

blocks.text: Endpoint records distinguish an inverted or shared axis from a threshold issue. Slow travel reveals whether Android reports genuine analog values or merely switches between zero and one. Removing the duplicate digital path prevents a light touch from becoming a full PS2 press.
Each trigger must rest released, progress predictably, and reach full activation independently.

items: L2 and R2 return to their released values.
Partial travel produces intermediate values when supported.
Full press reaches the expected endpoint.
Pressing one trigger does not move the other.
Reconnect preserves direction, range, and binding.
Both triggers share one signed axis: use the emulator's documented split-axis handling.
A trigger is digital only: document the limitation rather than inventing analog travel.
Values invert after a mode switch: return to the original controller mode.
Full range fails in Android's tester too: investigate firmware or hardware.

blocks.text: Return thresholds to default, restore the prior L2 and R2 entries, reconnect in the recorded mode, and verify ordinary digital actions. Keep experimental changes limited to this controller profile.
DualShock 2 pressure behavior extends beyond L2 and R2

Some PS2 games use pressure-sensitive face or shoulder buttons that modern controllers expose only digitally. Correct analog triggers do not automatically provide those other pressure values. Record whether Android reports each trigger as an independent axis, a shared signed axis, a digital button, or both. Never compensate for an inverted endpoint by adding a duplicate digital binding: verify released, partial, and full travel separately, then keep any unavoidable device limitation in the profile notes.
